title: Browser history and navigation basics
learningObjectives: Explain browser history and navigation basics and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: The History API exposes session history through history.back(), forward(), go(), pushState(), and replaceState(). pushState() changes the URL and adds a history entry without loading a new document; applications must update their UI and handle popstate navigation.
understand.whyItMatters: History management helps single-page navigation behave predictably. URLs should remain shareable and back/forward buttons should restore the expected view.
understand.analogy: Browser history is a trail of visited application states that lets a user retrace or revisit a step.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: pushState updates the URL and session history. It does not automatically render the new page or fetch content.

examples.explanation: pushState updates the URL and session history. It does not automatically render the new page or fetch content.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Build a tiny two-view navigation demo using pushState and popstate. Verify browser back and forward restore the view.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: Does pushState() automatically load a new document?
options: No, it changes the session history and URL without a document navigation
questions.answer: No, it changes the session history and URL without a document navigation
questions.explanation: pushState adds a history entry and updates the URL; the application must update its own view.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
